old_value: Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input; item presence alone never assumes stasis.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

item_identified.how: The leaf's old reason names the effect 'Time Stop'. Grepping the cached item corpus for 'Time Stop'/'stasis' yields exactly four items: 2420 Seeker's Armguard, 3026 Guardian Angel (Rebirth, not Time Stop), 3157 Zhonya's Hourglass, 228002 Wooglet's Witchcap. Wooglet's is withheld from an ordinary SR build by the cached modes table ('classic sr 5v5': false) and its acquisition note (requires the Arena augment 'Quest: Wooglet's Witchcap'). The Time Stop carriers legal on Summoner's Rift are Zhonya's Hourglass (3157) and its component Seeker's Armguard (2420) - both carry the identical Time Stop active text and the identical atom family declaration, so the analysis below holds for either.
item_identified.primary: 3157 Zhonya's Hourglass (Syndra is an AP mage; 3157 builds from 1058 + 2420)

facts: "passives": []  (the item declares NO passive effect at all)
"simpleDescription": "Activate to become invincible but unable to take actions"
step_1_effect_is_an_activated_ability_no.conclusion: Time Stop only occurs if the holder activates it. Possession of the item does not entail that the effect ever fires inside the priced fight window. This is exactly the old reason's second clause ('item presence alone never assumes stasis').

step_2_the_effect_has_a_fixed_bounded_du.quote: Put yourself in {{tip|stasis (buff)|stasis}} for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, rendering you {{tip|untargetable}} and {{tip|invulnerable}} for the duration but also unable to move, declare [[basic attack]]s, cast [[champion ability|abilities]], use [[summoner spell]]s, or [[active ability items|activate items]].
step_2_the_effect_has_a_fixed_bounded_du.conclusion: Duration = 2.5 s, fixed (no rank/level scaling in the cached text). A price for this effect is therefore a bounded active-seconds quantity, which the scenario must supply explicitly (how much of the 2.5 s window is spent inside the modeled fight). This is the old reason's first clause.

step_3_the_mechanic_DOES_change_outgoing.quote_wiki_atom: "description": "Full disable that also makes the unit invulnerable and untargetable; cannot be cleansed, unaffected by tenacity, disables even summoner spells."
step_3_the_mechanic_DOES_change_outgoing.reasoning: Stasis is classified in the cached vocabulary as a FULL DISABLE of the unit that holds it. The item text is explicit that the holder is 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items' for the duration. Over any fight window W that overlaps the stasis by t seconds (0 <= t <= 2.5), the holder's own damage output during those t seconds is zero. Outgoing total damage dealt therefore changes by -t * DPS - a first-order effect, not a durability-only effect.
step_3_the_mechanic_DOES_change_outgoing.conclusion: The new reason's clause 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD' is contradicted by the cached Wiki text. Stasis changes BOTH: durability up (invulnerable/untargetable) and outgoing damage down (full self-disable). This is precisely why the effect cannot be assumed from item presence and must be priced from an explicit bounded active-seconds input - assuming it silently would delete up to 2.5 s of the attacker's damage.

declared_atoms: family 'damage'                   | damage.resistance-mitigation  | Time Stop | relations: damage.damage-instance, damage.armor-penetration, damage.magic-penetration
step_4_not_every_declared_family_on_this.reasoning: The item declares three distinct families - 'stats', 'crowd-control-mobility', and 'damage' - and none of them is a 'defence' family. Two of the four declared atoms are non-defensive on their face: (a) stats.ability-power flat 105.0 is a purely OFFENSIVE stat, and (b) the Time Stop effect additionally emits an atom in the 'damage' family (damage.resistance-mitigation) whose relations point at damage-instance and both penetration atoms.

quantified_counterexample_for_this_scena.source: data/champions.json -> Syndra.abilities.Q[0] 'Dark Sphere', Magic Damage leveling modifiers: base [90,125,160,195,230] and [70,70,70,70,70] with units '% AP'
quantified_counterexample_for_this_scena.arithmetic: Zhonya's declared stats.ability-power = +105 AP; Dark Sphere AP ratio = 0.70 => outgoing damage per Q rises by 0.70 * 105 = 73.5 raw magic damage attributable to a family declared on THIS item.
quantified_counterexample_for_this_scena.conclusion: The item's own declared families raise outgoing damage by a computable, non-zero amount, so 'every declared family on this item is a defence ... not outgoing TDD' is false as written.

step_5_corroborating_grouping.conclusion: The cached economics table treats stasis as its own explicitly enumerated item class, consistent with stasis being priced as a named, explicitly-supplied quantity rather than folded into a generic 'defence' bucket.

verdict_rationale: The old string is fully consistent with the cached source: Time Stop is an activated, unique effect with a fixed 2.5 s duration, so its price is a bounded active-seconds quantity that the scenario must state, and mere possession cannot imply the stasis fired. The new string asserts two things the cached data contradicts: (1) 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' - the item declares families 'stats', 'crowd-control-mobility' and 'damage', including +105 flat ability power, an offensive stat worth +73.5 raw damage on a single Syndra Dark Sphere (0.70 AP ratio); (2) 'changes durability, not outgoing TDD' - the Wiki text and the stasis atom both state the holder is fully disabled and cannot attack, cast, or use summoners for the duration, which reduces outgoing damage by up to 2.5 s of output. The new reason also discards the operative modeling guard (presence != activation) that the old reason records.
